title: KV hit-rate stress plan and key-normalization advisor for safe TTL tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a practical, automatable workflow for recommending per-prefix TTL adjustments and cache-key normalization that balances cost savings with safety. Deliverables: a simulation harness for hit-rate shock testing, a canonicalizer for multi-model key variants, a staged TTL staircase rollout strategy, and automated rollback gating tied to real-time hit/latency regressions.
background: Current recommendations are fast-following: suggest aggressive TTL reductions for popular prefixes to reduce token cost. Production incidents over the last two quarters show some TTL changes caused downstream latency spikes due to unexpected cache miss cascades and model diversity (different canonical key formats per product). There is limited ability to pre-validate hit-rate impact under realistic synthetic traffic patterns that reflect prefix entropy and batching behavior.
proposal_summary: Build two coordinated components: (1) A stress-and-simulate harness that replays sampled request traces with configurable TTL stair-step policies and synthetic cache miss injection to estimate hit-curve and tail latency impact; (2) A key-normalization advisor that canonicalizes noisy cache keys (model-version tags, session tokens, prompt affixes) into stable prefixes, plus heuristics for safe prefix merging/splitting. Wire both into the recommendation engine so suggested TTLs come with a conservatism score and a recommended rollout ramp.
design_decisions:
- Use offline replay with shadowed synthetic load rather than only live small-canaries for initial scoring to avoid user impact.
- Stair-step TTL changes: apply 90%, 75%, 50%, 25% reductions with hold windows to observe delta before proceeding.
- Normalizer rulesets will be configurable per product; default rules include stripping ephemeral session ids, collapsing model aliases, and normalizing whitespace/token affixes.
- Conservative defaults favor increasing batching-friendly TTLs for requests with high sequence length variance.
tradeoffs:
- Offline simulation fast but incomplete (cannot capture cross-service backpressure). We'll mitigate by pairing with small live shadow canaries.
- Aggressive key merging reduces cardinality but risks semantic collisions; require manual review for high-impact prefixes.
- Running synthetic stress tests increases infra cost temporarily but avoids larger production regressions.
experiment_plan:
1) Collect a 48h sample of production requests (privacy-scrubbed) and extract prefix histograms, average seq lengths, and batch grouping characteristics.
2) Run replay baseline to establish current hit-rate and p95 latency.
3) For each candidate prefix, run 3 simulated TTL decks (25%,50%,75% reduction) with miss-injection at 0/1/5% to model cold-start storms.
4) Compute estimated cost delta, hit-rate delta, and p95 increase.
5) Rank prefixes by ROI while filtering out those with p95 impact > 10% or user-facing latency risk.
6) Generate recommended staircase rollout plan for each prefix with explicit hold durations and gating thresholds.
rollout_plan:
- Phase A (Shadow): deploy changes as shadow to 10% of traffic for 24h, collect real hit/latency deltas.
- Phase B (Staircase): apply TTL reduction to 25% of affected keys for 6h; if stable, escalate to 50% for 12h, then 100%.
- For multi-tenant prefixes, escalate per-tenant based on tenant-specific SLOs.
- All steps gated by automated checks (metrics listed below).
rollback_plan:
- Immediate automatic rollback if any gating threshold trips.
- Manual rollback path: on-call triggers rollback runbook (runbook link in attachments) that restores previous TTLs and replays failing segment in debug cluster.
- Postmortem: if auto-rollback occurs, run root-cause simulation and add prefix to manual-review list.
monitoring_and_metrics:
Primary gating metrics (evaluated every 5m window):
- prefix.hit_rate.delta_percent (alert if drop > 5%)
- global.p95_token_latency.delta_percent (alert if increase > 8%)
- downstream.queue_growth.rate (alert if sustained > 30% over 10m)
- error_rate.change (alert if increase > 2x baseline)
In addition report: estimated_cost_savings_per_hour, sampled_prefix_entropy, avg_batch_size_change.
risks_mitigations:
- Risk: noisy keys bypass normalization -> mitigation: add an approval step for keys with >1M cardinality.
- Risk: simulation misses cross-service tail effects -> mitigation: mandatory short live shadow for high-ROI prefixes.
- Risk: accidental semantic collapsing -> mitigation: conservative default rules and preflight tagging for manual review.
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulation harness can replay a 48h sample and output hit-rate delta and latency projection CSV.
- Key-normalizer can process live 1M keys/min and produce suggested canonical mapping with confidence scores.
- Automated recommendation UI exposes staircase rollout with gating thresholds and generates a staged job.
- Two successful internal canaries completed without auto-rollback and cost projection validated in billing sandbox.
notes: Targeting top 500 prefixes by spend first. We will maintain a conservative ‘do-not-touch’ list for prefixes that map to compliance-sensitive datasets. Coordinate with SEs for tenant-specific exemptions.
